subject: Private deployment upgrade — temporary control-plane connectivity issue & follow-up
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Maya Shah <maya@healthco.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment upgrade — temporary control-plane connectivity issue & follow-up

Hi Maya,

Quick note to let you know we observed a brief control-plane connectivity degradation in your private deployment during the scheduled agent upgrade we applied this morning (08:05 PDT). The user-facing inference surface was not impacted — models continued serving on active nodes — but the control channel to the private control-plane flapped for ~6 minutes which affected agent heartbeat telemetry and some console status updates.

What we did in the window:
- Triggered an automated rollback to the pre-upgrade control-plane image (08:11).
- Re-established agent heartbeats and cleared stale locks (08:16).
- Monitored the fleet for 30 minutes before declaring the environment stable (08:42).

We will share a short timeline and an initial post-incident summary once we've completed root-cause triage. Preliminary indication is an interaction between a newly-introduced connection pooling change and an older nginx sidecar configuration in your VPC that sporadically caused TLS session negotiation failures during bursts of reconciles.

Next steps from us:
1) Full timeline & root-cause analysis (target: EOD PST today) — attaching the raw timeline and debug logs in that follow-up.
2) A recommended mitigation bundle (config change + canary upgrade plan) and an optional maintenance window if you prefer we re-run the upgrade under our guidance.
3) A 30-min readout call tomorrow to walk through the RCA and planned remediation.

I realize any connectivity blip is frustrating — apologies for the interruption. Please let me know whether you want the upgrade retried during a maintenance window this week or prefer we pause until we deliver the complete postmortem.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwood.com]

[Attachment: incident-timeline.csv (csv)]

Subject: Re: Private deployment upgrade — temporary control-plane connectivity issue & follow-up

Thanks for the heads-up, Jordan.

We'd like the readout tomorrow at 09:00 PDT if that works for your team. If there are any critical mitigations you recommend before a reattempt, call them out in the summary and we can approve a short maintenance window.

-Maya

maya@healthco.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment upgrade — temporary control-plane connectivity issue & follow-up

Jordan — logging quick notes from triage:
- Root cause (prelim): a regression in connection pooling introduced in v2.4.1 of the control-plane agent. Under burst reconciles we observed >200 simultaneous TLS renegotiations; older nginx sidecars with keepalive_timeout < 65s dropped connections during the handshake window.
- Why rollback worked: rolling back to v2.4.0 reverts the pooling heuristic; fewer renegotiations and existing TLS sessions persisted.
- Short-term remediation we can recommend to HealthCo: increase keepalive_timeout on sidecars to 120s and apply a max_conns cap on control-plane listener to smooth bursts.

I'll assemble the debug traces and add the packet-level capture to the timeline. Sending Jordan the draft summary and logs for review.

-Marcus

[Attachment: controlplane-debug.log (log)]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Maya Shah <maya@healthco.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Sep 2026 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-incident summary: control-plane connectivity regression (private deployment)

Hi Maya,

Attached is our post-incident summary and the timeline from the upgrade yesterday. TL;DR: a control-plane agent pooling change in 2.4.1 triggered TLS session churn under reconcile bursts with older nginx sidecars; we rolled back to 2.4.0 and validated stability.

What we included in the packet:
- One-page summary (attached) with impact, timeline, RCA, and recommended mitigations.
- Raw timeline (CSV) and debug logs for your compliance records.
- A proposed mitigation plan if you want to re-run the upgrade: 1) bump sidecar keepalive_timeout to 120s, 2) run a 10% canary in a non-production slice for 24 hours, 3) monitor heartbeat and TLS error rates, 4) roll forward with staged increases.

Suggested immediate actions for HealthCo (you can opt in or we can apply with your approval):
- Apply sidecar config change (keepalive_timeout=120s).
- Allow Redwood to run a canary upgrade during a mutually agreed maintenance window (we'll handle canary telemetry and rollback hooks).

Proposed readout call: Mon 09/20 09:00 PDT (30 minutes) — I set a provisional invite but can reschedule.

Attachments: redwood-postmortem-summary.pdf, incident-timeline.csv, controlplane-debug.log

Apologies again for the disruption. We're adding a gating test in our release pipeline (TLS-session-saturation sim) to catch this class of regression before releases.

Regards,
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: redwood-postmortem-summary.pdf (pdf)]

From: Maya Shah <maya@healthco.com>

Thanks, Jordan — the summary looks good and includes the level of detail our audit requires. We'll apply the sidecar keepalive change in our staging cluster this afternoon and confirm telemetry. The 09:00 PDT readout on Mon works for us.

Please include an ops-runbook snippet in the final postmortem that spells out the rollback procedure and the tracing commands our on-call should run. We'll want that in the ticket for our internal audit.

-Maya
